We have 13C NMR: signals at 168.20, 134.30, 131.90, 128.20 (x2), 127.40 (x2). That's 7 distinct carbons. Aromatic ring has 6 carbons, plus one carbonyl (C=O) at 168 ppm typical for an ester or carboxylic acid? 168 ppm could be carbonyl of an ester (C=O of CO2R) or amide? For benzoic acid, carbonyl ~170-173 ppm. For benzaldehyde, carbonyl ~190-200 ppm. For acetophenone, carbonyl ~200? Actually acetophenone carbonyl ~200. For benzoic acid ~170. For methyl benzoate (ester) carbonyl ~166-170. So 168 suggests a carbonyl attached to aromatic, likely a carboxylic acid or ester. The aromatic carbons: typical chemical shifts: ipso carbon attached to carbonyl ~135, ortho ~129, meta ~128, para ~127. The pattern matches.

Thus likely compound is benzoic acid (C6H5COOH) or methyl benzoate (C6H5COOCH3). But we have only 7 carbons total, which matches both: benzoic acid (C7H6O2) has 7 carbons. Methyl benzoate also C8H8O2 (8 carbons). So 7 carbons indicates benzoic acid. Also 1H NMR shows only aromatic protons (5 total). Benzoic acid has OH proton maybe broad, but may be exchangeable and not observed. So 5 aromatic protons: pattern of monosubstituted benzene: 2H doublet of doublet? Actually typical pattern: 7.5-7.9 region with multiplets. The given: 2H dddd at 7.47, 3H tt at 7.64. That matches benzoic acid.

Thus SMILES: O=C(O)c1ccccc1 (or "OC(=O)c1ccccc1"). Standard SMILES: "O=C(O)c1ccccc1". Provide final answer.

Check with get_formula_from_smiles to confirm formula C7H6O2. Could validate.
